title: Houden van en lekker vinden
summary: houden van, vinden, graag — three ways to say you like something — plus lekker as universal approval

blocks.title: Drie manieren om iets leuk te vinden
blocks.body: **houden van** (to love/really like) is strong and lasting. **vinden** (to find/think) states an opinion about one specific thing. **graag + werkwoord** (gladly) says you like *doing* something.

blocks.title: lekker: het woord voor alles
blocks.body: *lekker* starts as 'tasty' but it's really Dutch's all-purpose word of approval: *lekker weer* (nice weather), *lekker slapen* (sleep well), *lekker bezig!* (doing great!). If something is good, it's *lekker* — food or not.
blocks.callout: You'll hear *lekker* about ten times before lunch. That's normal.

pairs.right: vinden — an opinion about this one thing
pairs.note: *Ik houd van kaas* is a standing fact about you. *Ik vind deze kaas lekker* is a verdict on the piece in front of you.

blocks.prompt: Which sentence correctly means 'I like eating fries'?
blocks.explain: *graag* slots in right after the finite verb: *Ik eet graag patat* — verb second, *graag* third.
*Ik houd van kaas* — *hou* is the everyday spoken contraction of *houd*, both are fine.

blocks.prompt: Listen and type what you hear.

blocks.title: Say what you like
blocks.prompt: Build a sentence about something you like.
Tell me three things you like — use houden van, vinden…lekker, and graag once each.
